Surfaced by the `os-dev` on objectui#9511 while executing ruling batch #195 item 1. ⛔ Filed rather than left as an Acceptance note because the fallback does not hold: the re-dispatched PR **will be in this file**, but it ⛔ **cannot fix these** — no ruling reaches them ⇒ no carrier.

## The claim — the ruling's enumeration is INCOMPLETE, so 「one rule, no exception」 has survivors

Ruling batch #195 item 1 (`5749154869`) extends 「a record id is a **string** wherever metadata names one」 to `CommentEntry.recordId` and `MentionNotification.recordId` as 「the same principle」. But **two more published interfaces in the very same file** carry the identical spelling and are named by **no ruling and by no comment on that card**:

| interface | `recordId` | published? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CommentSearchResult.recordId` | **REQUIRED** (⛔ not optional) `string \| number` | re-exported from `@object-ui/types` via the `./views.js` export list; present in built `dist/views.d.ts` |
| `RecordSubscription.recordId` | **REQUIRED** `string \| number` | same |

Seat-verified on `origin/main` `0c2eb5eee0`: `packages/types/src/views.ts` carries **5** occurrences of `recordId: string | number`; `CommentSearchResult` 1 hit, `RecordSubscription` 4, `CommentEntry` 3, `MentionNotification` 1. **[ABSENT CTRL]** `zzNoSuchInterface` → 0, so the ruler reads this file.

⇒ by the ruling's own principle the enumeration is **10 published declarations** in `packages/types/src`, ⛔ not 8.

## Third site, same decision

`DataSourceMutationEvent.id` in `packages/types/src/data.ts` is still declared `string | number` — the sixth site on the published `DataSource` surface, already flagged as never named by any ruling in the 2026-09-17T20:09Z comment on objectui#9511 and confirmed still present today. ⭐ Folded in here so **one** decision covers all three survivors rather than three cards arriving separately.

## Why this matters more than three type annotations

Class **(b)** — a published contract disagreeing with a rule the project has already adopted. ⚠️ The failure mode is specific: a rule stated as universal, with quiet exceptions left in the same file, teaches an author (and an AI) that the spelling is a matter of taste. That is worse than never having stated the rule.

## What triage should settle

Whether the maintainer's 「one rule, no exception」 reaches these three. It is a **ruling-scope** question, ⛔ not an implementation one — if yes, it is three one-line narrowings plus their fallout; if no, the exceptions need to be stated as exceptions where an author reads them.
